overview.headline: How water circulates between ground and atmosphere through key processes

keyPoints.point: Students learn that the hydrologic cycle involves continuous circulation of water between ground and atmosphere.
keyPoints.quote: The hydrologic cycle involves the continuous circulation of water in the Earth-Atmosphere system.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that evaporation requires energy to change liquid water into gas.
keyPoints.quote: For evaporation to take place, energy is required.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that transpiration is evaporation of water from plants through stomata.
keyPoints.quote: Transpiration is the evaporation of water from plants through stomata.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that condensation changes water vapor into liquid and appears as clouds or dew.
keyPoints.quote: Condensation is the process whereby water vapor is changed into a liquid state.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that runoff collects in rivers and lakes and evaporation of that water begins the hydrologic cycle over again.
keyPoints.quote: Evaporation of this runoff into the atmosphere begins the hydrologic cycle over again.

keyTerms.gloss: change of state from liquid to gas that requires energy to occur
keyTerms.quote: For evaporation to take place, energy is required.

keyTerms.gloss: evaporation of water from plants through leaf openings called stomata
keyTerms.quote: In most plants, transpiration is a passive process largely controlled by the humidity of the atmosphere and the moisture content of the soil.

keyTerms.gloss: process where water vapor changes into liquid forming clouds or dew
keyTerms.quote: water vapor has a higher energy level than that of liquid water, when condensation occurs,

keyTerms.gloss: water that falls to earth when condensation particles grow too large to stay aloft
keyTerms.quote: Runoff occurs when there is excessive precipitation and the ground is saturated (cannot absorb any more water).

keyTerms.gloss: excess water that cannot be absorbed by saturated ground and flows into rivers and lakes
keyTerms.quote: Rivers and lakes are results of runoff.
